title: Assignment 2 · Streaming sketches
summary: Work the DGIM, Flajolet–Martin, and AMS questions as distinct stream queries with explicit memory and error contracts.
objectives: Compute the Flajolet–Martin estimate from a hash observation
Derive and average AMS second-moment estimates

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Assignment 2 supplies the exact window, repeated-value stream, and estimator calculations; MMDS supplies the stream-query and sketch invariants as labeled depth.

sections.title: DGIM is a recent-window count
sections.body: DGIM stores timestamped buckets of 1s with at most two buckets of each size. When a query cuts through the oldest bucket, count it fractionally to expose the approximation error instead of pretending the boundary is exact.

sections.title: Different sketch, different target
sections.body: Flajolet–Martin estimates distinct elements from the longest zero-prefix in hashed values. AMS estimates a frequency moment such as $F_2=\sum_i f_i^2$ from position samples. They are not interchangeable just because both use bounded memory.

math.name: Second frequency moment
math.purpose: State the target estimated by AMS.
math.explanation: The second moment $F_2=\sum_i f_i^2$ weights repeated values quadratically, so a stream with one 1, two 2s, and three 3s already has a different target from its distinct count.

contrastDrills.prompt: A DGIM query window cuts through one bucket. Which bucket is the boundary bucket that may need fractional counting?
choices: The oldest bucket that overlaps the window boundary
The newest bucket, because it was created last
Any bucket with size 1, regardless of timestamp
No bucket; DGIM counts every bucket exactly
contrastDrills.explanation: Buckets are timestamped. The oldest bucket that is only partly inside the queried window is the uncertain boundary; DGIM counts it fractionally to expose approximation error.
contrastDrills.misconception: Choosing the newest bucket because it is visually prominent, or treating the oldest partially covered bucket as fully inside.
contrastDrills.repair: Mark the time-window boundary first, then identify the oldest bucket crossing it and apply the stated fractional rule.

contrastDrills.prompt: A stream contains values with frequencies 3, 2, and 1. What are the zeroth moment and the total number of stream elements?
choices: Both moments equal 3 because there are three values
contrastDrills.explanation: The zeroth moment $F_0$ counts distinct values, so it is 3. The first moment $F_1=\sum_i f_i$ counts all occurrences, so it is $3+2+1=6$.
contrastDrills.misconception: Calling the number of distinct keys the total stream length, or treating every frequency moment as a square-sum.
contrastDrills.repair: Ask whether the target counts distinct identities ($F_0$) or sums their frequencies ($F_1$) before selecting a sketch.
